name: Rikaitan/Yomitan
description: mouse over vocab and kanji for readings, definitions, and morphology

notes.text: Great for automatically creating Anki flashcards from vocab you encounter in the wild! Even if you don't use Anki (you should!), this is the fastest and best (tbh) way to look up vocab in browser.
For Anki integration: from Anki, install the
AnkiConnect
addon in order to allow Rikaitain to create Anki cards. This is also doable on mobile, see
this guide!

name: Anki
description: Spaced-repetition system (SRS) flash card program

notes.text: The BEST flash card/SRS platform around. You can study pre-built decks like Kaishi 1.5k, or build your own decks (e.g. with Rikaitan!).  If you are beginner, start with a beginner vocab deck! If you are intermediate but find your vocab lacking, it is worthwhile downloading a vocab deck, then browsing the cards and "suspending" all of the vocab you already know by heart (or just relearn them for practice.) If you are more upper intermediate, it is recommended to mine your own vocab from native content, but you may find some prebuilt decks useful.
How to Use Anki
Kaishi 1.5k Basic Vocab Deck
Beginner's Vocab from Anime Deck

Anki is free on desktop and Android (AnkiDroid), but for a free iOS app you may have to hunt around. The official app on iOS is paid, but you can also access your decks and do reviews from Safari by going to
ankiweb.net

.
It may be easier to search for prebuilt decks via Google/Reddit/etc. than it is to use Ankiweb's built-in search.

name: jpdb.io
description: Comprehensive dictionary; pre-generated vocab decks for books/anime; SRS platform

notes.text: More thorough than most dictionaries in that it compiles lots of info about every word or kanji. Includes kanji decompositions, example sentences, examples words that use a particular kanji, example kanji that use a kanji, frequency info, ...
See for example:
解読-Vocab
and
解-Kanji
. You can even search for an anime and see full vocab lists for each episode, e.g.
here

! About jpdb's SRS platform - it could kind of be an Anki alternative, if you really don't want to use Anki. it automatically teaches you dependencies of a word before that word, including kanji components. For example, before teaching you 読解, you will learn 言,売,読; and 角,刀,牛,解. (It gets much more granular than that actually). Also, it tracks what you know across decks, which is super neat!
There are decks for Genki and Minna no Nihongo if you happen to be learning using one of those!

name: Ttsu Reader
description: E-book reader for web browsers (enables Yomitan/Rikaikun etc lookups for e-books!)

notes.text: Upload your e-book (it stays local) and you can read it in browser. Reading in-browser enables dictionary lookups with browser add-ons like Rikaitan/Yomitan, making it easy to add flashcards to Anki for example.
